subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should maintainers split this mixed report into broad backed-follow-up enforcement and a separate exec/process termination policy, and what default should OpenClaw enforce for each?
rationale: Source inspection shows real gaps, but mutating final replies and deciding whether to block or steer broad shell kill commands are product and safety-policy choices rather than a narrow mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Split And Define Both Policies
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers route the follow-up behavior to the canonical backed-follow-up tracker and define the supported exec/process kill path for OpenClaw-managed sessions.

options.title: Only Track Follow-Up Policy
options.body: Treat the follow-up loop as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58450 and ask for a new focused exec report if the `pkill` failure reproduces on current main.

options.title: Add A Narrow Exec Guard First
options.body: Prioritize a small guard or prompt change around self-matching `pkill -f` commands, then leave broader reply enforcement for later product review.

recommendation.title: Split And Define Both Policies
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers route the follow-up behavior to the canonical backed-follow-up tracker and define the supported exec/process kill path for OpenClaw-managed sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The follow-up-policy side is the higher-risk product decision and builds on prior reminder/commitments work attributed to this owner.
